summary: A collection of recent research papers on AI models, covering topics like manipulation agents, multimodal models, and time series analysis. The papers address challenges like data scarcity, sim-to-real transfer, and efficient reasoning.
intended_use_and_workflow: The models are intended for various applications, including robotics, tool use, video generation, dialogue generation, and medical decision-making. The workflows typically involve training, fine-tuning, and evaluation on specific tasks.
model_limitations: Identified limitations include scarcity of high-quality multimodal trajectories, difficulties in transferring policies from simulation to the real world, and performance deficits in long-chain reflective reasoning.
model_type: Includes vision language models (VLMs), multimodal large language models (MLLMs), diffusion models, reinforcement learning (RL) models, and time series foundation models.
training_data: The training data varies depending on the model and task. It includes automatically generated demonstrations, multimodal datasets, pre-trained vision encoders connected with pre-trained LLMs, interaction data generated by the agent's own actions, and data from the MIMIC-IV database.
validation_test_dataset: The models are evaluated on a variety of benchmarks, including Agent-X, GTA, GAIA, MM-HELIX, BLiMP, EWoK, Winoground, VQA, and datasets from various search agent benchmarks.
